sections.title: Appendix C-2 Definition of Terms: asphalt base course–micro-surfacing
sections.summary: Term range 'asphalt base course' to 'micro-surfacing' from Appendix C-2 (Definition of Terms): 11 pavement engineering terms specific to this UFC's non-universal usage, including definitions and, for percent VFA/VMA/VTM, their basic bitumen/air/aggregate volumetric-ratio formulas.
sections.body: Section C-2 (Definition of Terms) of Appendix C defines terms used in this UFC that are not universally accepted or have limited usage elsewhere; common AC pavement terms are not repeated here since they are covered in general flexible pavement references, primarily ASTM D8. This range runs alphabetically from 'asphalt base course' through 'micro-surfacing', covering 11 defined terms, including the percent VFA, VMA, and VTM void-content definitions expressed as simple volumetric ratios of a compacted bituminous mixture (bitumen, air, and aggregate volumes).
key_points: asphalt base course: A minimum of one course of asphalt mixture placed on a subbase or subgrade to serve as a base course (called a black base); covered with an intermediate course and surface course.
coarse aggregate: The aggregate retained on the 4.75-millimeter (No. 4) sieve as described in ASTM E11.

cold-mix recycling: Reclaiming existing bituminous pavement by breaking it to a maximum particle size of 4 cm (1.5 in.), mixing with virgin materials if needed, and reusing as pavement material for secondary road surfacing (with a seal coat) or as a base course for high-quality pavements.
components of a compacted bituminous mixture: A given volume of compacted bituminous concrete consists of air, bitumen, and aggregate.
fine aggregate: Aggregate passing the 4.75-millimeter (No. 4) sieve and retained on the 75 um (No. 200) sieve, often called sand; natural sand is found naturally, not manufactured by crushing.
flow: The deformation, measured in 0.25 mm (0.01 in.) units, of a compacted paving-mixture specimen at the point maximum load begins to decrease during the Marshall stability test.

hot-mix recycling: Removing existing HMA, crushing it, and mixing it in a hot-mix plant with new aggregate, asphalt, and recycling agent as required; the recycled HMA is designed for use in all pavement types, and crushed PCC has also been used as aggregate in hot recycled mixtures.
intermediate course: The pavement layer placed on the base course as a leveling/transition layer between the base and surface courses; also called a leveling or binder course.
Marshall stability value: The maximum load in newtons (pounds) applied to an AC paving-mixture specimen when tested in the Marshall apparatus.
mastic asphalt: An HMA mixture of fine aggregate and asphalt cement forming a mixture free of voids.

micro-surfacing: Applying a latex-modified asphalt emulsion slurry to an existing pavement surface, similar to slurry seals but with specially designed mixing/constant-agitation equipment for the latex modifier and larger aggregate particles; used to fill ruts or re-establish skid resistance, cur...
sections.applicability: Consult when looking up the specific meaning of a pavement term in the range 'asphalt base course' to 'micro-surfacing' as used in this manual.

sections.title: Appendix C-2 Definition of Terms: mineral filler–warm-mix asphalt
sections.summary: Term range 'mineral filler' to 'warm-mix asphalt' from Appendix C-2 (Definition of Terms): 11 pavement engineering terms specific to this UFC's non-universal usage, including definitions and, for percent VFA/VMA/VTM, their basic bitumen/air/aggregate volumetric-ratio formulas.
sections.body: Section C-2 (Definition of Terms) of Appendix C defines terms used in this UFC that are not universally accepted or have limited usage elsewhere; common AC pavement terms are not repeated here since they are covered in general flexible pavement references, primarily ASTM D8. This range runs alphabetically from 'mineral filler' through 'warm-mix asphalt', covering 11 defined terms, including the percent VFA, VMA, and VTM void-content definitions expressed as simple volumetric ratios of a compacted bituminous mixture (bitumen, air, and aggregate volumes).
key_points: mineral filler: Mineral aggregate particles passing a 75 micrometer (No. 200) sieve, or commercially available materials such as lime or cement.
optimum asphalt content: The asphalt content of a paving mixture, determined by Marshall or gyratory design methods, that satisfies the applicable pavement mix design criteria.
percent VFA: Percentage of the VMA (voids in mineral aggregate) in the compacted aggregate mass that is filled with asphalt: VFA = [v_bitumen / (v_air + v_bitumen)] x 100.
percent VMA: Percentage of the compacted bituminous mixture not occupied by the aggregate: VMA = [(v_air + v_bitumen) / v_total] x 100, i.e. percent VTM plus percent asphalt cement by total volume.
percent VTM: Percentage of the compacted AC mixture not occupied by the aggregate or asphalt cement: VTM = (v_air / v_total) x 100.

porous friction course (PFC): An open-graded, free-draining asphalt paving mixture placed on an existing pavement to minimize hydroplaning and improve wet-weather skid resistance, typically 20 to 25 mm (3/4 to 1 in.) thick; produced in asphalt hot-mix plants and placed with conventional asphalt p...

resin-modified pavement (RMP): A composite pavement surfacing combining HMA and PCC materials in the same layer: an open-graded AC mixture with 25 to 35 percent voids filled with resin-modified Portland cement grout, 5 cm (2 in.) thick, with a surface appearance similar to rough-textured PCC.

stone matrix asphalt (SMA): Also called stone mastic asphalt: a mixture of aggregate, mineral filler, polymer-modified asphalt cement, and a mineral or cellulose fiber, designed to prevent rutting and abrasion under high loads or high tire pressures.
surface course: The top course of an AC pavement, also referred to by many pavement engineers as the wearing course.

surface recycling: Repaving, heater-planing-scarifying, cold milling, and rejuvenating methods used to increase skid resistance, decrease permeability to air/water, and improve asphalt binder properties, modifying 5 to 50 mm (1/4 to 2 in.) of the pavement surface; does not increase pavement stren...
warm-mix asphalt: Asphalt mixture treated through additives or foaming to allow mixing, placing, and compacting at lower temperatures than HMA.
sections.applicability: Consult when looking up the specific meaning of a pavement term in the range 'mineral filler' to 'warm-mix asphalt' as used in this manual.
